sourcedFrom: 702 and 715T PLINKSTER® — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 17928, typeset 2/15/18 (2018 (typesetting stamp 2/15/18 on every page; no separate copyright line is printed))
cleanIntro: A rimfire semi-auto gets dirtier faster than anything else you own, and Mossberg says so — clean it every 200 rounds. The strip is two takedown screws to get the barrelled action out of the stock, two pins to drop the trigger housing, then the bolt up and out through the ejection port.

steps.title: Magazine out, then the chamber cleared and the bolt locked open
steps.action: Drop the magazine first, then pull the operating handle fully rearward to extract and eject anything in the chamber, and push the handle inward to lock the bolt open. This rifle fires with the magazine out if a round is chambered — that is printed on its own page in this book — so the magazine coming out proves nothing on its own.
steps.aside: Push the operating handle inward to lock the bolt in the open position.
steps.quote: Pull the operating handle fully rearward to extract and eject any cartridge that might be in the chamber.
steps.cite: 702 and 715T PLINKSTER® — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 17928, typeset 2/15/18 — DISASSEMBLY FOR CLEANING AND LUBRICATION, p.13

steps.title: Safety fully right, then prove the chamber empty by eye and finger
steps.action: Move the safety button fully right to ON, then look into the chamber and the receiver and put a finger in. A .22 case is small, dull and easy to overlook against a dirty receiver — touch settles it. Eye protection on before the bolt spring comes out.
steps.aside: Visually and physically inspect the chamber and inside the receiver to be certain the firearm is unloaded.
steps.quote: Move the safety button fully to the right to the “ON” (SAFE) position.
steps.cite: 702 and 715T PLINKSTER® — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 17928, typeset 2/15/18 — DISASSEMBLY FOR CLEANING AND LUBRICATION, p.13

steps.title: Two takedown screws, and the barrelled action lifts out of the stock
steps.action: A No. 2 Phillips takes the two takedown screws in the stock, one at the front of the trigger guard and one behind it. Lift the barrel and receiver away from the stock as a unit. Keep the screws together — they are the parts that loosen with use, and this manual asks you to check them at every cleaning.
steps.quote: Using a No. 2 Phillips screwdriver, remove the two takedown screws located at the front and back of the trigger guard and pull the barrel/receiver assembly away from the stock.
steps.cite: 702 and 715T PLINKSTER® — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 17928, typeset 2/15/18 — DISASSEMBLY FOR CLEANING AND LUBRICATION, p.13

steps.title: Two trigger housing pins out — mind the finish
steps.action: Drift the two trigger housing retaining pins out of the sides of the receiver with a pin punch that fits. Work on a supported surface and do not let the punch skate — the black finish on these parts marks easily and the manual asks you to be careful with it specifically.
steps.quote: With a pin punch or similiar tool, remove the two trigger housing retaining pins located at the side of the receiver (Fig. 12).
steps.cite: 702 and 715T PLINKSTER® — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 17928, typeset 2/15/18 — TO DISASSEMBLE THE FIREARM, p.15

steps.title: Housing out while you hold the bolt back, then ease the bolt forward
steps.action: Hold the operating handle fully rearward and lift the trigger housing out of the receiver. Then let the handle move forward SLOWLY under control — letting the bolt slam home with the trigger group out is how the buffer and the bolt face get battered.
steps.aside: Allow the operating handle to SLOWLY move fully forward.
steps.quote: While holding the operating handle fully rearward, carefully lift the trigger housing from the receiver (Fig. 13).
steps.cite: 702 and 715T PLINKSTER® — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 17928, typeset 2/15/18 — TO DISASSEMBLE THE FIREARM, p.15

steps.title: Bolt buffer out of the back of the receiver
steps.action: Take the bolt buffer out of the rear of the receiver and note which way it faces. It is a small part with an orientation and no obvious keying, and it is the one people put back reversed and then wonder why the bolt feels harsh at the end of its travel.
steps.quote: Remove the bolt buffer from the rear of the receiver (Fig. 14).
steps.cite: 702 and 715T PLINKSTER® — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 17928, typeset 2/15/18 — TO DISASSEMBLE THE FIREARM, p.15

steps.title: Bolt handle out through the ejection port — watch the pinch
steps.action: Pull the bolt back with the operating handle until you can get a forefinger in front of it, lift slightly, and take the bolt handle out through the ejection port. Keep your finger clear of the gap between bolt face and barrel as it comes — a bolt spring driving a bolt onto a fingertip is the injury this step is written to avoid.
steps.quote: Be careful not to pinch your finger between the bolt face and the barrel.
steps.cite: 702 and 715T PLINKSTER® — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 17928, typeset 2/15/18 — TO DISASSEMBLE THE FIREARM, p.16

steps.title: Bolt up and out, then its spring and guide rod
steps.action: Keep lifting on the bolt while letting it come forward against the barrel, get a finger through the ejection port and manoeuvre the bolt assembly up and out. The bolt spring and its guide rod come off separately — keep them paired, they go back into the bolt as an assembly.
steps.aside: Remove the bolt spring and bolt spring guide rod (Fig. 17a).
steps.quote: Maneuver the bolt assembly completely up and out of the receiver.
steps.cite: 702 and 715T PLINKSTER® — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 17928, typeset 2/15/18 — TO DISASSEMBLE THE FIREARM, p.16

steps.title: Field strip complete — the owner's work stops here
steps.action: Stock, trigger housing, buffer, bolt and its spring. That is everything this manual asks an owner to take apart, and it says so in one sentence. The trigger housing is not opened and the bolt is not stripped further; anything past this goes to the factory service centre or a gunsmith.
steps.quote: No further disassembly should be done by the owner.
steps.cite: 702 and 715T PLINKSTER® — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 17928, typeset 2/15/18 — TO DISASSEMBLE THE FIREARM, p.16

steps.title: Rimfire interval: every 200 rounds, not every season
steps.action: Semi-autos need cleaning more often than manual actions, and a .22 semi-auto is the dirtiest of the lot — unjacketed lead and waxy lube put residue everywhere. Mossberg's interval is 200 rounds, sooner in dust or wet or with ammunition that leaves heavy fouling.
steps.aside: Your firearm should be inspected and cleaned after every 200 rounds to ensure that it remains in good condition.
steps.quote: Semi-automatic firearms require more frequent cleaning than those manually operated.
steps.cite: 702 and 715T PLINKSTER® — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 17928, typeset 2/15/18 — CLEANING AND LUBRICATION, p.17

steps.title: Bolt, feed ramp and receiver — residue here is what jams it
steps.action: Work the bolt's sliding surfaces, the feed ramp and the inside of the receiver until they are free of solid residue. On a blowback .22 this is the difference between a rifle that runs and one that short-strokes: solid residue can stop the bolt closing fully, and a misfire follows.
steps.quote: The bolt and the receiver must be carefully cleaned and free of any solid residues.
steps.cite: 702 and 715T PLINKSTER® — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 17928, typeset 2/15/18 — CLEANING AND LUBRICATION, p.17

steps.title: Barrel from the muzzle — so protect the crown
steps.action: This barrel cannot be cleaned from the breech, so the rod goes in at the muzzle and the crown is at risk every stroke. Guide the rod, keep it centred and do not let it rub the edge. A .22 brass brush with solvent, then dry patches until they come out clean, then one lightly oiled patch.
steps.quote: As it is not possible to clean the barrel from breech to muzzle, be very careful while introducing the cleaning rod into the barrel muzzle, thus avoiding any damage to the barrel crown.
steps.cite: 702 and 715T PLINKSTER® — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 17928, typeset 2/15/18 — THE BARREL, p.17

deepAbsentReason: The manual ends the owner's teardown in one sentence — "No further disassembly should be done by the owner. If service is required, contact the factory authorized service center or a qualified gunsmith." The trigger housing is never opened and the bolt is not stripped beyond its spring and guide rod, so there is no deeper published procedure to author for this rifle.

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: .22 brass brush with solvent, several passes
Dry patches until they come out clean, then one lightly oiled patch
Rod goes in at the muzzle on this rifle — protect the crown every stroke

cleaning.name: BOLT & RECEIVER
tasks: Bolt sliding surfaces and the feed ramp free of solid residue
Inside of the receiver wiped out; light oil only
Bolt spring and guide rod wiped and kept together

cleaning.name: TRIGGER HOUSING
tasks: Brush loose residue away — the housing is not opened
No heavy oil in here; it collects the next 200 rounds' worth of fouling

cleaning.name: SCREWS & FASTENERS
tasks: Check the two takedown screws at each cleaning — this manual asks for it
Do not over-tighten the Plastite screws or the magazine release screw

reassembly: Bolt spring and bolt spring guide rod into the bolt assembly.
Bolt into the receiver bolt-face first, then the operating handle through the ejection port to line up with its slot in the bolt.
Compress the bolt spring and lower the bolt into the receiver, keeping the operating handle in position, until the end of the guide rod pops into the blind hole at the rear of the receiver.
Bolt buffer back in, oriented as it came out.
Bolt pushed fully rearward and held there; trigger housing into the receiver; then let the bolt come SLOWLY forward.
Line the housing holes up with the receiver holes and insert both retaining pins.
Barrelled action into the stock and both takedown screws tightened — one behind the trigger guard, one in front of the magazine.
fncheck: Magazine out, action open, chamber checked, muzzle safe. Close the action with the safety ON and pull the trigger fully: the hammer must not fall. Take your finger off, move the safety to OFF: it must still not fall. With the safety OFF, pull the trigger — now it should fall. Finish by locking the bolt open and putting the safety back ON. If it behaves any other way, contact the Product Service Center instead of loading it.
